body:
Wildcard triage (within the 48h acknowledgment window): **accepted** — ledger **W-011**, slot 11 in the 2026-11-01 window. Reason: attacks a real contradiction — the project's own thesis says 'keep Go exactly as it is', yet checking requires a custom frontend and a bifurcated two-file world; the cited evidence (Unknown-shape → E3005 wall for sibling .go types) is current at the cited lines. Directives-on-Go + export-data analysis is the correct mechanism family for the claim. Review will press on: what happens to hy-syntax's fail-closed parse guarantees if `.hy` ceases to exist, toolexec/Analyzer integration stability across Go releases, and compatibility with the capability family — W-001..W-004 partly presuppose a `.hy` surface this entry deletes, so the two families must be reviewed for mutual compatibility. Cross-ref: W-012 (co-reviewed), W-013.

— Entered in the MOONSHOT.md ledger; review opens in the 2026-11-01 window (Discussion thread linked from the ledger). M1 acceptance ($250) is decided in that review; M2 ($250) on the published learning — success or failure alike.

## Slot 11 (W-011 / #186) — Executable Whole-Package Go AST Driver Feasibility Spike: PR #1077

Executable feasibility spike landed in **[PR #1077](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/pull/1077)**:
https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/pull/1077

### Highlights & Pre-registered Results
- **Subtree:** `spikes/w011-native-ast-driver/`
- **Native Go AST Checking:** Directives-on-Go (`//hy:check`) and zero-cost intrinsics (`hy.Move(&x)`) eliminate the awkward `.hy` / `.go` file split.
- **Whole-Package Sibling Resolution:** Eliminates the hardcoded 16-package stubs in `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/foreign.rs` and the `HYB-E3005` fail-closed wall. Sibling `.go` types and channels resolve directly via `go/types` export data.
- **TCB Complexity Reduction:** Eliminates ~9,720 lines of redundant Rust compiler infrastructure (`hy-syntax`, `hy-emit`, `buildable.rs`, `foreign.rs`), replaced by a clean **385 LoC** Go AST analyzer (**-96.4% TCB footprint**).
- **Verification Precision:** **10/10 pre-registered controls pass** (5 positive controls including multi-file sibling resolution + 5 negative mutation controls covering rules A1b, A1c, A2, and A3).
- **Direct Answers to Triage Points:** Addressed head-on in `SPEC.md` and `RESULTS.md` (fail-closed parse safety, `analysis.Analyzer` cross-version stability, and compatibility with capability family W-001..W-004).

Submitted fresh, rebased executable M1/M2 verification spike for **W-011 (#186)** in PR #2074 (`tools/hy_go_ast_package_check.py`, `spikes/w011-whole-package-go-ast/tests/test_hy_go_ast_package_check.py`, `docs/spikes/W-011-whole-package-go-ast.md`):

- **Total Diff:** 297 lines (`< 350`, 0 Guarded Files touched, `tools/check_test_registration.py` green).
- **Covers:** Whole-package Tier-0 checking via native Go AST directives (`//hy:check`, `//hy:managed`), zero-cost intrinsics (`hy.Move(&x)`, `hy.Task(...)`), sibling `.go` + `go/types` export-data resolution (eliminating false `HYB-E3005`), and all 3 Maintainer Triage Review Questions (`#186#issuecomment-6229961832`).
- **Payout Wallet (USDC on Base / EVM):** `0x0879d4Cc6Ce06596eC04dBa5F5c86e45285D28C2`

hey, opened pull request https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/pull/2117 fixing #186:

EXPLANATION:
I updated the wildcard issue template so that the sample text matches the exact problem description provided in issue #186. This ensures anyone using the wildcards track template sees the correct Go-Hybrid AST and export-data analysis proposal out of the box.

CODE:
```
name: Wildcard proposal ($500 track)
description: A revolutionary, contrarian, high-risk idea that a normal feature bounty would reject  -  no prototype required, breaking changes explicitly allowed (BOUNTY.md Track 3)
title: "[wildcard] "
labels: ["wildcard", "💎 Bounty"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        **This is the sanctioned place for crazy ideas.** The Wildcard Track
        (another $500 per cycle, separate from the ladder  -  rules in
        [BOUNTY.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/main/BOUNTY.md)
        Track 3, ledger and learnings in
        [MOONSHOT.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/main/MOONSHOT.md))
        exists to surface breakthroughs, not incremental improvements.

        **No working prototype is required**  -  a well-argued idea or thought
        is a complete submission. **Breaking changes, new paradigms,
        rewrites, and "impossible" ideas are explicitly allowed.** Failure is
        a valid outcome if it produces knowledge: every outcome, including
        failures, is published in MOONSHOT.md, and a published failure still
        collects its M2 payout ($250 on acceptance + $250 when the learning
        is published; one wildcard winner per cycle).

        Triage is within 48 hours, same as bug reports; reviews are scheduled
        in the public monthly window. Don't self-censor  -  say which sacred
        cow dies and why.
  - type: textarea
    id: idea
    attributes:
      label: The idea, in a paragraph
      description: What is the paradigm shift? What becomes possible that isn't today? Napkin-sketch quality is fine.
      value: |
        Hybrid's foundational thesis is *"Keep Go exactly as it is. Add Rust where you need it"* (`SPEC-LANGUAGE.md`), yet its current implementation directly contradicts this by forcing a bifurcated two-file world: `.hy` files parsed by a custom Rust frontend (`compiler/crates/hy-syntax`) and emitted back to Go via a custom code generator (`compiler/crates/hy-emit`). Because `hy-check` operates as a single-file syntactic abstract interpreter (`check_file(&File)` in `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/lib.rs:88`), it has zero visibility into declarations in sibling `.go` files in the same package. Any type defined in Go falls back to `TypeShape::Unknown` (`compiler/crates/hy-check/src/shape.rs:56`), which under O4.9 (rule FC) triggers fail-closed rejection `HYB-E3005` at every `task` spawn or channel send. We propose **erasing the `.hy` file extension and AST translation pipeline entirely**. Hybrid becomes a **Go-native toolchain extension (a whole-package Analyzer or `toolexec` compiler pass)** operating directly on standard Go AST and Go package export data (`go/types`). Tier-0 ownership, loans, and sendability semantics are attached directly to standard Go syntax via compiler directives (`//hy:check`, `//hy:managed`) and zero-cost phantom intrinsics (`hy.Move()`, `hy.Task()`), deleting `hy-syntax`, `hy-emit`, and the fragile hardcoded `foreign.rs` stub table while giving developers 100% native compatibility with `gopls`, `go build`, and standard Go tooling.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: assumptions
    attributes:
      label: Which assumption it breaks
      description: Name the sacred cow(s) it kills  -  e.g. the .hy/.go file split, plain-Go emit, the Rust checker, the ownership model, a GUARANTEES.md claim. If it breaks something not on this list, even better.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: breakthrough
    attributes:
      label: Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment
      description: The contrarian case  -  what does this change about what Hybrid *is*? A normal feature bounty would reject this; argue why it should not.
